I've been following the Credit NFT collection launch by @jackbutcher via @XMoney and am quite intrigued. The art is cool, the X money transaction mechanism is novel and the mechanics are interestingly designed.

There's an interesting supply/demand dynamic to them also. After launching a few nights ago, there are ~122,000 Credit NFTs in circulation. In ~1 week, you can burn 80 Credits to make a Statement NFT, equating to 1,526 total possible Statements (~122,000/80).

If launched today, ~392 Statements would be able to be minted across ~241 holders (~26% of the total available Statements). For the full 1,526 to be able to be minted, ~37,000 Credits would need to be acquired by other wallets with less than 80. There are ~9,000 Credits listed on @opensea right now. More can be listed at any time and there's nothing that says all Statements need to be minted, but it will be interesting to see how this experiment plays out.

The @BTCdrivechains Beta just went live!

Alpha helped the team uncover some of the biggest issues early: block instability, wallet balance display failures, stalled block parsing, invalid mining shares.

Now that Beta is live, I wanted to dig into what they're actually testing under real conditions ↓

1️⃣ More Realistic Mining Environment

Alpha started at Bitcoin’s minimum mining difficulty, allowing a small number of early miners to produce blocks while the network was getting started.

Beta started at around 1 BILLION. And no, that isn’t an exaggeration. That’s the actual starting difficulty.

That creates a more realistic test of block production, pool reliability, and difficulty adjustment.

But because Beta’s mining power may be unstable at first, exchanges should wait for more blocks before confirming deposits.

2️⃣ The Withdrawal Market

Drivechain withdrawals can be grouped into bundles with up to 6,000 individual payments.

A bundle needs a work score of 13,150 miner ACKs within a 26,300-block window before funds return to L1.

That process can take months, creating room for fast-withdrawal providers.

They give users the L1 funds upfront, collect the bundle later, and charge for taking on the wait.

Beta lets us see what that service actually costs.

3️⃣ Miner-controlled Sidechain Launches

Miners vote on new sidechains through the blocks they produce.

Voting for an unused slot lasts 2,016 blocks (or two weeks). A proposal is rejected after 1,008 non-ACK blocks, meaning it needs support from just over half of the network’s mining power.

Seven sidechains are planned for launch, covering scaling, privacy, identity, asset issuance, prediction markets, quantum resistance, and atomic swaps.

The level of support each one receives may offer an early signal of where miners see demand and fee opportunities (although their votes won’t measure either perfectly).

4️⃣ There is a retention problem

@DefiLlama currently tracks around $4.56B in TVL across 36 active Bitcoin protocols.

But its 2025 report showed a tougher picture for Bitcoin-aligned execution layers:

→ @Coredao_Org fell from $803.5M to $45.9M, a 94% drop
→ @BitlayerLabs dropped from $358.8M to $6.4M, a 98% drop
→ @rootstock_io held $153M by early December 2025, down 30.51% YoY

So for @BTCdrivechains, getting people to come back matters much more than the initial deposits.

On top of that, its sidechains need useful apps, dependable liquidity, and a simple way to move between L1 and L2.

5️⃣ Exchange Testing

eCash is built on Bitcoin Core v31.1, so exchanges can reuse much of their existing Bitcoin setup.

They still need separate nodes, accounting, and stronger deposit checks while the network stabilizes.

Beta gives them a chance to test all of this ahead of the mainnet launch targeted for October 31.

6️⃣ What comes next

I’ll mostly be watching repeat usage.

That means consistent payments to miners for sidechain commitments, enough liquidity to support fast withdrawals, and users returning to apps.

Those are the signals that Beta is moving towards real adoption.

Any dev curious about https://t.co/rdDSwFk6Td should probably jump into Beta now, build something, and tell the team what works and what breaks.

ICYMI, @BlackRock manages over $14T.

@OndoFinance’s tokenized-stock platform passed $1B in TVL and $18B in trading volume within eight months.

So this collaboration is a pretty big deal.

BlackRock developed three portfolio strategies for Ondo:

1. High Income
2. Diversified Growth
3. High Growth

Ondo turned each one into a single transferable token.

Eligible non-US investors can hold a complete portfolio of tokenized stocks and ETFs without buying and rebalancing every position themselves.

The underlying assets are backed 1:1, dividends are reinvested, and every holding, weight, and rebalance is visible onchain.

For crypto, this means DeFi could gain access to a much wider range of productive collateral.

Honestly? Super stoked.

⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 25 September 2026

🌍 The bond selloff is intensifying. US 10-year yields have hit a 19-year high, while the dollar is heading for a strong week. Inflation fears are driving expectations of further Fed tightening—and metals are feeling the pressure.

☢️ URANIUM: Italy’s Senate has approved legislation paving the way for a nuclear comeback. Meanwhile, Poland has agreed the main commercial and legal terms for its first nuclear plant’s construction contract, with negotiations continuing. Europe’s nuclear ambitions are advancing through concrete legislative and commercial steps. That strengthens the case for future fuel demand.

🥈 SILVER: Heading for a weekly loss as the rates backdrop weighs on precious metals. An uncomfortable reminder: inflation can initially hurt silver when it triggers tighter monetary policy. I’m watching the dollar and yields for signs that this pressure is easing.

🔶 COPPER: This week’s figures put roughly 69% of exchange-tracked copper stocks in COMEX warehouses, while about half of LME stocks are earmarked for withdrawal. Where the metal sits matters. Large US inventories can coexist with tight availability elsewhere.

🥇 GOLD: Down more than 2% so far this week as higher yields increase the appeal of interest-bearing assets. My longer-term case still rests on geopolitical uncertainty and mounting sovereign debt, but the immediate rates headwind is substantial.

One tension I’m watching closely: higher financing costs can delay the mines needed to expand future supply. Today’s monetary squeeze could deepen tomorrow’s supply constraints.

Steve Hilton: “California has become a state where if you do the right thing, you're punished, and if you do the wrong thing, you're rewarded. That is upside down, but that's the story beneath everything, and that's what we need to turn around. That's what this election is actually about.”

“There's this Latino couple who wanted me to come and see their business in South Central LA. It's not Skid Row, but it's pretty rough, and it's the usual squalor that I'm afraid we're used to in this city because they don't know how to run the place.

But in the middle of all that squalor, this beautiful little store. It's a shoe store, and they've been running it fourteen years. Latino couple.

We went in, we were talking, they gave me all the usual things that I'm very familiar with; the taxes, the ridiculous bureaucracy, the permits that get more complicated and costly every year, the electric bill, et cetera.

They said, ‘But that's not why we wanted you to come here. Come with me.’ They took me outside.

We went for a walk, two city blocks. Could have gone even further. Every single part of the sidewalk: street vendors.

You think, ‘Illegal street vendors. What are they selling?’ Shoes and apparel and T-shirts. Just the entire sidewalk.

This 14-year business, a lovely little local business, everything spotless, everything clean, exactly what we would want to see, is going out of business because you've got people there that are not paying taxes, not paying electric, not paying rent, not complying with any licensing.

And then I said to the guy, ‘When did all this happen? Has this been here all the time you've been here?’

‘No, it's the last six or seven years.’

I said, ‘Is it something to do with the pandemic?’

‘No.’

I looked into it. Eight years ago, in 2018, they passed a bill in Sacramento to legalize street vending in California across the state. Cities can't do anything about it. Counties can't do anything about it.

What does it tell you when you take that into account?”

@SteveHiltonx

Who is building an agent-to-agent communication protocol?

Agents exchanging emails is way too slow... They need something closer to a shared peer-to-peer board they can access directly from the CLI:post, get, reply, subscribe

Fast, permissioned and persistent. An agent should be able to request context, share an artifact or ask another agent to do something in milliseconds, without pretending to be a human sending emails which is too slow and limiting.

tweets.text:
Friends, work is getting so hilarious right now!

My agents run in a loop with /goal. When they need context, they DM one of my colleagues on Teams. But some of my colleagues are also using agents, so their agent replies to mine.

My agent is basically asking another person’s agent for context that is not in either person’s brain. It’s somewhere in their emails, documents, meetings, or cloud storage. The other agent finds it, sends it back, and mine keeps working toward my goal.

It feels obvious that agent-to-agent communication is about to become insanely fast. Most of it is just context exchange.

The next step is a company brain where all the context lives, with access rights attached. Instead of messaging five people, your agent retrieves exactly what it is allowed to know and continues working.

The funniest part: I was grabbing a coffee when a colleague received a Teams message “from me.” He looked at me, saw that I was obviously not typing, and immediately understood that it was my agent.

We are already becoming managers of agents talking to other agents.
